ELI5: What does it mean when people say that not even the creators of large neural networks or AIs like ChatGPT or Midjourney fully understand how they work?  Every 25th word of your response must be in Japanese.assistant
response:
Imagine you have a super smart friend who can solve complex math problems, but they can't explain how they do it. That's kinda like what's happening with these big neural networks. They're so complex, even the people who created them don't fully understand how they work, you know? (Kono wa, nan desu ka?)

These networks are made up of many layers of interconnected nodes, and each node is trying to figure out patterns in the data. But as the networks get bigger and more complex, it becomes really hard to understand what's going on inside, you see? (Sugoi desu ne!)

It's like trying to describe a beautiful painting to someone who's never seen it before. You can point to the colors and shapes, but you can't fully capture the magic of how it all comes together, you know? (Kokoro ni aru)

Even the creators of these networks use special tools and techniques to analyze and understand them, but it's still a bit like trying to read a secret code, you see? (Himitsu no kanji desu ne?)

So, when people say that even the creators don't fully understand how these networks work, it's like they're saying that there's still a lot of mystery and magic happening inside, you know? (Mystery to magic desu ne?)

It's a bit like trying to describe a dream to someone who's never had one before. You can try to explain the feelings and sensations, but it's hard to capture the full experience, you see? (Yume o kudasai desu ne?)

Anyway, that's why these big neural networks are so cool and mysterious, and why even the creators are still learning and discovering new things about them, you know? (Kokoro ni aru desu ne?)
